title: Lattice structure of linear congruential generators: RANDU's 15 planes, an exact spectral test with the coset correction, and Monte Carlo integrals and physical simulations that the lattice breaks
summary: We computed the exact spectral test in exact integer arithmetic (LLL reduction followed by exhaustive Fincke-Pohst enumeration) for RANDU (65539), RANDM (6539), MINSTD (16807), MINSTD2 (48271) and the mixed LCG 69069, for t = 2 to 8. We then checked every prediction by enumerating all tuples of the full period (2^29 to 2^32 of them) in Fortran, and every predicted largest gap was reproduced to 7 significant digits. For m = 2^31 with a = 3 (mod 8) the reachable states are only x = x0 or 3x0 (mod 8). The correct lattice therefore has modulus 2^30, not 2^31 or 2^29, and the true largest empty slab sometimes comes from a family of planes with two offsets: it is 1.34 times wider than 1/nu_t for RANDU at t=2 and for RANDM at t=3. On the course question, RANDU and RANDM fail in opposite places. RANDU is good in 2D (S_2 = 0.66) but has only 15 planes in 3D (9x_k - 6x_{k+1} + x_{k+2} is an integer, S_3 = 0.0095). RANDM is the worst of the five in 2D (6539 lines, S_2 = 0.19) but reasonable in 3D to 8D (818 planes in 3D). Using the shortest dual vectors we built integrands with exact integral 0 that every LCG estimates as exactly 1 with zero sample variance (z = 4472 at N = 10^7), while MT19937 and RANNUM pass. RANDU also biases three physical simulations. An ideal gas built from its triplets shows a Bragg peak S(9,-6,1) = N. Directions drawn by cube rejection put 13.75% of all directions on one great circle, and none fall in the band 0 < |cos theta| < 0.184. The estimate of pi from the volume of the unit ball converges to 3.15432, the 15-plane quadrature value, instead of pi (+59.8 sigma at 2x10^8 triplets).

methods.name: Exact spectral test
methods.description: For a multiplier a and effective modulus M, the dual lattice is L*_t = {s in Z^t : s_1 + a s_2 + ... + a^{t-1} s_t = 0 (mod M)}, with basis (M,0,...,0) and (-a^{j} mod M) e_1 + e_{j+1}. We reduce the basis with LLL (delta = 99/100), using exact rational Gram-Schmidt in Python Fractions. Fincke-Pohst enumeration then lists every lattice vector with |s|^2 <= |b_1|^2. The interval bounds come from float square roots widened by one and each candidate is rechecked exactly, so no vector can be missed. Outputs are nu_t^2 = min |s|^2, all shortest vectors s (the plane normals), the distance 1/nu_t between adjacent covering hyperplanes in the unit cube, the normalized figure of merit S_t = nu_t / (gamma_t^{1/2} M^{1/t}) with exact Hermite constants (gamma_t^t = 4/3, 2, 4, 8, 64/3, 64, 256 for t = 2..8), and Knuth's mu_t = pi^{t/2} nu_t^t / (Gamma(t/2+1) M). The implementation was validated against brute-force search over all integer vectors in the Hermite ball for 48 random (a, M, t) cases, with M in {1009, 1024, 2039, 4096} and t = 2..5.
methods.parameters: t = 2..8; RANDU a=65539 and RANDM a=6539 with M = 2^30 (coset lattice, see next method), MINSTD a=16807 and MINSTD2 a=48271 with M = 2^31-1, LCG69069 a=69069, c=1, M = 2^32 (full-period mixed generator). Runtime 4 s in total.

methods.name: Coset correction and exact largest gap for m = 2^e, a = 3 (mod 8)
methods.description: With an odd seed x0, the subgroup generated by a in (Z/2^e)^* is {u = 1 or 3 mod 8}, so the 2^{e-2} reachable states are y = x0 or 3x0 (mod 8). The t-tuples y(1,a,...,a^{t-1}) mod 2^e are therefore two cosets of the lattice L_8 = {8k v} + 2^e Z^t. The smallest lattice coset containing them has dual {s.v = 0 mod 2^{e-1}}, so uniform plane families must be computed with modulus 2^30, not 2^31. For a general integer normal s, let g = s.v mod 2^e and k = v_2(g). The values s.X mod 2^e then lie in the two cosets x0 g + H and 3 x0 g + H with H = 2^{min(k+3,e)} Z. The largest cyclic gap gives h(s) = 1 for k >= 30, 1/2 for k = 29, and 6*2^k/2^e for k <= 28. The width of the largest empty slab orthogonal to s is h(s)/|s|. The true largest gap d_t = max_s h(s)/|s| was found by enumerating, for each k, every s in the modulus-2^k dual lattice with |s| < h_k nu_t(2^30). The theory was validated by brute force over all integer normals for every tuple of the full period, for e = 9..12 (36 cases, 0 mismatches).
methods.parameters: e = 31, x0 = 777 (the result does not depend on which odd seed is used); conventions with modulus 2^31, 2^30 and 2^29 are reported side by side.

methods.name: Full-period exhaustive plane enumeration (lat_verify.f90)
methods.description: Each LCG is re-implemented with integer(8) arithmetic and cross-checked against rnglib for 10^6 steps. The program then walks the complete period, forms every overlapping t-tuple of integer states (cyclically), and computes r = s.X exactly for every predicted normal s. It records the set of residues r mod M, every occupied plane (distinct value of r), the population of each plane, and the largest gap between adjacent occupied planes, converted to unit-cube distance gap/(M|s|). It also checks that the state returns to its start after P steps and not after P/2.
methods.parameters: Full periods: RANDU and RANDM 2^29 = 536870912 tuples, MINSTD and MINSTD2 2^31-2, LCG69069 2^32. 43 normal vectors in total (shortest vectors, the true-largest-gap vectors, and the naive modulus-2^31 vectors). CPU time 36 to 226 s per generator, about 8.4 min in total.

methods.name: RANDU plane test and plane populations
methods.description: For 10^7 overlapping and 10^7 non-overlapping triplets (seed 777) we check exactly that 9X_k - 6X_{k+1} + X_{k+2} = 0 (mod 2^31) and record the plane index j = (9X_k - 6X_{k+1} + X_{k+2})/2^31. The expected share of plane j is p_j = f_S(j), where f_S is the density of S = 9U_1 - 6U_2 + U_3 for iid uniforms. Its cross-sectional area is |n| f_S(j), and the lattice point density per unit area is the same on every plane. p_j is computed exactly by inclusion-exclusion and comes out as (1,3,5,7,9,11,12,12,12,11,9,7,5,3,1)/108, with sum exactly 1 (a B-spline partition of unity). The statistic is a Pearson chi-square with 14 dof on the non-overlapping counts. The floating-point view histograms S = 9x-6y+z computed from REAL(8) outputs, and from REAL*4 outputs via rng_single, in 0.01-wide bins on [-6, 10]. MT19937 and RANNUM serve as controls, using the fraction of triplets with |S - nint(S)| < 0.005 (expected 0.01).
methods.parameters: N = 10^7 triplets per variant; full-period populations from lat_verify (2^29 triplets).

methods.name: Edge-on projections
methods.description: Non-overlapping t-tuples are projected onto u = s.x/|s| (distance along the plane normal) and onto v = w.x, where w is the diagonal (1,...,1) with its s component removed. The 3D RANDU view uses an orthographic camera whose viewing direction d = (0.4946, 0.7988, 0.3420) satisfies d.(9,-6,1) = 0 exactly (azimuth 58.24 deg, elevation 20 deg). For RANDM we plot pairs with x_k < 3/6539 among 10^8 pairs, and triplets in a slab of width 8/|s| around s.x/|s| = 0.6 with s = (25,115,678).
methods.parameters: 20000 tuples per gallery panel, 12000 triplets in each 3D panel, seed 777; MT19937 uses the same projections as the control.

methods.name: Killer integrands (Monte Carlo integration that fails)
methods.description: For a dual vector s with plane offset phi (s.x = phi mod 1 for every tuple), f_s(x) = cos(2 pi (s.x - phi)) has exact integral 0 over [0,1]^t, since any nonzero integer frequency integrates to zero. A lattice generator gives f_s = 1 for every tuple. We estimate the integral from N non-overlapping t-tuples and report the running mean, the sample standard error, and z = mean/(1/sqrt(2N)), which uses the true null standard deviation 1/sqrt(2) of cos(2 pi U). All 7 generators were crossed with all 8 integrands. The offsets phi come from the residues found by the exhaustive enumeration: 0, 1/2 for RANDM's modulus-2^30 vectors, and 1917898033/2^32 for LCG69069. For RANDM's two-offset family (58,-375,-69) we also computed the complex mean of exp(2 pi i s.x).

methods.name: Structure factor of a simulated ideal gas
methods.description: N particles are placed in the periodic unit box at r_j = (x_{3j+1}, x_{3j+2}, x_{3j+3}). For every integer wave vector n with |n_i| <= 10 we compute S(n) = |sum_j exp(2 pi i n.r_j)|^2 / N. For an ideal gas S(n) is approximately Exp(1) for n != 0, while a crystal gives Bragg peaks S = N. Note that S(s) = N |mean exp(2 pi i s.x)|^2, the same quantity as the killer integral. Statistics are the maximum over the 4630 independent wave vectors (half space; expected maximum about ln 4630 + 0.577 = 9.0) and a KS test of the non-Bragg values against Exp(1).
methods.parameters: N = 10^5 particles; RANDU, RANDM, MINSTD, MT19937, RANNUM; seed 777.

methods.name: Isotropy of emission directions
methods.description: Directions are generated by the standard cube-rejection method: v = 2u - 1 from non-overlapping triplets, accepted if 0 < |v| <= 1, then d = v/|v|. As a 2D control we also use the (cos theta, phi) method with cos theta = 2u_1 - 1 and phi = 2 pi u_2. cos theta is measured relative to n = (9,-6,1)/sqrt(118) and histogrammed in 400 bins, and an equal-area sky map in (phi, cos theta) uses 144 x 72 cells. Statistics are Pearson chi-square against uniformity (399 and 10367 dof), the fraction of directions with |cos theta| < 10^-12, and the count in the band 0.005 < |cos theta| < 0.18. Theory for RANDU: in [-1,1]^3 the planes 9x-6y+z = 2j-4 lie at distances d_k = 2k/sqrt(118), k = -5..5, inside the unit ball. A plane at distance d contributes density proportional to d^2/c^3 for |c| >= d, which gives f(c) = (2/W) sum_{0<d_k<=|c|} d_k^2/|c|^3 plus a point mass 1/W at c = 0, where W = sum_k (1 - d_k^2) = 7.2712. The fraction is also computed exactly over the full period.
methods.parameters: 2x10^6 directions per method; RANDU cube, MT19937 cube, RANDU (cos theta, phi), RANDM cube; seed 777.

methods.name: pi from the volume of the unit ball, with block and seed controls
methods.description: Estimator pi_hat = 6 x (fraction of triplets with |2u-1| <= 1), with binomial standard error 6 sqrt(p(1-p)/N). For a lattice generator the estimate is a quadrature over its planes. For RANDU the limit is 6 pi h sum_k (1 - d_k^2)/8 with plane spacing h = 2/sqrt(118). The cube cross-sections sum exactly to the cube volume, while the ball's sum to 4.2058 instead of 4 pi/3. Controls: the exact full-period count for RANDU and RANDM. Block dispersion of hit counts (variance over binomial) uses blocks of 10^4 to 10^7 triplets over 1.79x10^8 triplets, with chi-square of (n-1)D on n-1 dof. A seed scan covers 48 seeds (odd seeds 1..47 and 24 random large odd seeds), giving the z at N = 10^7.
methods.parameters: N up to 2x10^8 triplets for RANDU, RANDM, MINSTD, MT19937, RANNUM; blocks for all 7 generators.

findings.claim: Every RANDU triplet lies exactly on one of 15 planes 9x_k - 6x_{k+1} + x_{k+2} = j, j = -5..9, separated by 1/sqrt(118) = 0.0921 in the unit cube.
findings.evidence: In integer arithmetic, 9X_k - 6X_{k+1} + X_{k+2} was divisible by 2^31 for all 10^7 overlapping and 10^7 non-overlapping triplets from seed 777. Over the full period (2^29 triplets) exactly 15 planes are occupied and the largest gap is 9.205746e-2 = 1/sqrt(118). In REAL(8) the computed S = 9x-6y+z is an exact integer for every triplet, so the fraction with |S - nint S| < 0.005 is 1.000000. The same fraction is 0.009956 for MT19937 and 0.009953 for RANNUM (expected 0.01, binomial sigma 3.1e-5, so -1.4 and -1.5 sigma). The algebra: a = 2^16 + 3 gives (a-3)^2 = 2^32 = 0 (mod 2^31), so X_{k+2} = 6X_{k+1} - 9X_k (mod 2^31).

findings.claim: The populations of the 15 RANDU planes are exactly what the geometry predicts: plane j carries the share f_S(j) = (1,3,5,7,9,11,12,12,12,11,9,7,5,3,1)/108, where f_S is the density of 9U_1 - 6U_2 + U_3.
findings.evidence: For 10^7 non-overlapping triplets, chi-square = 11.55 on 14 dof (p = 0.64), with max |z| = 2.13 on plane j = 7. Overlapping triplets give chi-square = 6.52 (p = 0.95), but those counts are dependent. Over the full period the counts differ from 2^29 f_S(j) by at most 608 (relative 1.2e-4, on the outermost planes) and by 2 or less on the central planes, which is lattice discretization at the polygon edges.

findings.claim: Storing RANDU in single precision does not remove the planes; it only thickens them by about 3e-7, which is 3.4e-6 of their spacing.
findings.evidence: With rng_single = .true. (outputs rounded to REAL*4), the largest |9x-6y+z - nint| over 10^7 triplets is 3.13e-7 (the a priori bound is 16 x 2^-25 = 4.8e-7). 7.6% of the residuals are exactly 0 and the typical size is 1e-7. All 10^7 triplets still have |S - nint S| < 0.005. In REAL(8) the residual is exactly 0.

findings.claim: The exact spectral test makes RANDU the worst (generator, dimension) pair of all 35 tested: S_3 = 0.0095, and S_t <= 0.26 for t = 4, 5, 6. In t >= 4 the shortest dual vector is (9,3,-5,1), giving 17 hyperplanes spaced 0.0928, slightly wider than in 3D. RANDU is good in 2D (S_2 = 0.658).
findings.evidence: nu_t^2 = 536936458, 118, 116, 116, 116, 116, 116 for t = 2..8. S_t = 0.658, 0.0095, 0.050, 0.137, 0.261, 0.410, 0.566. Knuth mu_3 = 5.0e-6 and mu_4 = 6.2e-5 (the pass threshold is 0.1). Marsaglia's upper bound for t = 3, m = 2^31 is (3! m)^{1/3} = 2344 planes, while RANDU uses 15. The family (9,-6,1,0,...) also gives 15 planes in every t >= 4, but with the smaller spacing 0.0921. Full-period enumeration reproduced every gap (empirical/predicted = 1.000000).

findings.claim: For m = 2^31 and a = 3 (mod 8) (both RANDU and RANDM), the spectral test must be applied to the coset lattice with modulus 2^30. Even then 1/nu_t can underestimate the true largest empty slab, because families of planes with two offsets per period can be wider. Neither the naive modulus 2^31 nor the reduced modulus 2^29 is exact.
findings.evidence: The reachable states are x0 or 3x0 (mod 8) (2^29 of them), which is half of a coset of the modulus-2^30 lattice. Naive modulus 2^31: RANDM nu_3^2 = 1610846 against the correct 473534, and nu_6^2 = 1394 against 402, which overstates the quality. Modulus 2^29: RANDM 1/nu_7 = 0.0707 against the true largest gap 0.0696, and 1/nu_5 = 0.0178 against 0.0166, which overstates the gap. The true largest gap exceeds 1/nu_t(2^30) for RANDU t=2: 5.790e-5 against 4.316e-5 (x1.34, normal (3,-1), h = 3/16384). It also does so for RANDM: t=3, 1.945e-3 against 1.453e-3 (x1.34, normal (58,-375,-69), offsets 5/8 and 7/8); t=6, 0.0593 against 0.0499 (x1.19); t=7, 0.0696 against 0.0602 (x1.16). The theory matched brute force in 36 of 36 small-modulus cases, and the full-period enumeration reproduced each of these gaps to 7 digits.

findings.claim: The exact spectral-test code and every one of its 43 plane predictions were confirmed by exhaustive full-period enumeration and by brute force.
findings.evidence: Brute force agreed in 48 of 48 cases (M up to 4096, t <= 5). Full-period enumeration covered 2^29 (RANDU, RANDM), 2^31-2 (MINSTD, MINSTD2) and 2^32 (LCG69069) tuples. Every tuple lies on the predicted residue classes, with no overflow of the residue table. For all 43 normals the empirical largest gap divided by the predicted one is 1.000000, and every period check passed. Occupied plane counts can be one less than the number of planes that geometrically meet the cube (RANDM t=6: 43 occupied of 44), because the corner planes contain no lattice points. Our nu_t^2 for 69069 (4243209856, 2072544, 52804, 6990, 242) and for 16807 (282475250, 408197, 21682, 4439, 895), t = 2..6, are the values we recall from Knuth's Table 1 in Sec. 3.3.4; we did not check them against the book.

findings.claim: The 'small but significant' difference between RANDM (6539) and RANDU (65539) is that they fail in opposite dimensions. RANDM is the worst of the five LCGs in 2D: every pair lies on 6539 lines 6539x_k - x_{k+1} = j, and x_{k+1} = 6539 x_k exactly whenever x_k < 1/6539. From 3D up, however, RANDM is far better than RANDU.
findings.evidence: RANDM: S_2 = 0.186 with line spacing 1.529e-4, 5.4 times the optimal 2.84e-5 for modulus 2^30; mu_2 = 0.125, which barely passes Knuth's 0.1. Of the 46014 pairs with x_k < 3/6539 among 10^8, every one lies on 3 lines. In 3D, 25x_k + 115x_{k+1} + 678x_{k+2} lies in Z + 1/2 on 818 planes (spacing 1.45e-3, true largest gap 1.94e-3), so S_3 = 0.599 (0.447 using the true gap), comparable to MINSTD (0.441) and 61 to 47 times RANDU's 0.0095. Planes for t = 4..8: 277, 111, 43, 35, 33 (RANDU: 17 in each). RANDM's weakest point above 2D is t = 6: S_6 = 0.486, normal (3,6,-8,-14,9,-4), offset 1/2. RANDU: S_2 = 0.658 but S_3 = 0.0095. The reason for RANDM's 2D weakness is that 6539 < sqrt(2^30) = 32768, so (6539,-1) is a short dual vector. RANDU fails because (a-3)^2 = 0 (mod 2^31).

findings.claim: Every LCG has an elementary integrand with exact integral 0 that it estimates as exactly 1, with zero sample variance, at every sample size. Each such integrand fails only for its own generator.
findings.evidence: For each owner pair (RANDU with (9,-6,1); RANDM with (6539,-1), (25,115,678) and the 6D vector; MINSTD with (16807,-1) and the 8D vector; MINSTD2 8D; LCG69069 6D) the estimate is 1.00000000 with standard error 0.0 at every checkpoint from N = 10 to 10^7, which gives z = sqrt(2N) = 4472 at N = 10^7. The 48 off-diagonal z values have mean -0.13, variance 0.87 and max |z| = 2.70, consistent with N(0,1). MT19937 and RANNUM pass all eight integrands with |z| <= 2.11. For RANDM's two-offset family (58,-375,-69), over 10^6 triplets the mean of cos is 0.00000 and the mean of sin is -0.70711 = -1/sqrt(2), as the coset theory predicts.

findings.claim: Standard Monte Carlo error bars cannot reveal a lattice failure. For the killer integrands the estimated standard error is exactly 0, so the naive analysis reports the wrong answer with infinite confidence.
findings.evidence: The sample variance of f_s is 0 for the owner generator at every N, while the true standard deviation under uniformity is 1/sqrt(2) = 0.707. Only an external reference (exact value 0, or a second generator) exposes the error.

findings.claim: An ideal gas simulated with RANDU positions diffracts like a crystal: the structure factor has a Bragg peak S(9,-6,1) = N, while all other wave vectors behave like an ideal gas.
findings.evidence: With N = 10^5 particles, S(9,-6,1) = 1.000000e5 exactly. Over the other 4629 wave vectors with |n_i| <= 10 the maximum is 9.13 (expected maximum of Exp(1) about 9.0), and a KS test against Exp(1) gives p = 0.30. Controls: MT19937 max 8.82 (KS p = 0.033), RANNUM 9.30 (p = 0.99), RANDM 9.10 (p = 0.57). RANDM and MINSTD show no peak in this window because their shortest 3D dual vectors (25,115,678) and (90,-44,631) lie outside it, which is a resolution limit of the test. At those vectors the killer integrals give S = N.

findings.claim: The largest non-Bragg structure-factor value, MINSTD S(1,-10,2) = 15.49, is a statistical fluctuation and not a generator flaw.
findings.evidence: The chance of a maximum of at least 15.49 among the 23150 values examined (5 generators x 4630) under Exp(1) is 4.4e-3. The value does not persist: it is 10.4 at N = 3x10^5 and 1.82 at N = 10^6 from the same seed. Five further disjoint blocks of 10^5 particles give 0.05 to 6.66, and five other seeds give 1.02 to 2.12. MINSTD has no dual vector near (1,-10,2) (its shortest 3D vector has norm 639).

findings.claim: Isotropic emission simulated with RANDU and cube rejection is grossly anisotropic. 13.75% of all directions lie exactly on one great circle (the plane orthogonal to (9,-6,1)), and the adjacent belt 0 < |cos theta| < 2/sqrt(118) = 0.184, which covers 18.4% of the sphere, receives no directions at all.
findings.evidence: Of 2x10^6 directions, 276278 (13.81%) have |cos theta| < 1e-12, against the theory 1/W = 0.137529 and the exact full-period value 38816731/282243511 = 0.13752922. The band 0.005 < |cos theta| < 0.18 contains 0 directions against 350000 expected (MT19937: 349762). Over the full period no in-ball triplet falls in the band. Chi-square on cos theta (399 dof) is 1.37e7, or 6.1e5 with the central bins removed, and chi-square on the sky map (10367 dof) is 2.45e6. The 15-plane sawtooth density f(c) = (2/W) sum d_k^2/|c|^3 matches the histogram bin by bin, for example 1.415 predicted against 1.412 observed just above |c| = 0.184. Controls: MT19937 cube rejection gives chi-square = 422 (p = 0.20) and sky p = 0.37. RANDU with the 2D (cos theta, phi) method passes (chi-square = 433, p = 0.12; sky p = 0.97), because RANDU's 2D lattice is good. RANDM cube rejection also passes (chi-square = 363, p = 0.90).

findings.claim: Hit-or-miss Monte Carlo of the unit-ball volume with RANDU converges to the wrong value, 3.15432 instead of pi (+0.40%). The cause is that RANDU's 3D Monte Carlo is really a 15-plane quadrature rule.
findings.evidence: pi_hat = 3.154259 +- 0.000212 at N = 2x10^8 non-overlapping triplets (z = +59.8). The exact full-period value is 6 x 282243511/2^29 = 3.1543170 (z = +98 at the full period with iid errors). The plane-sum prediction 6 pi h sum(1-d_k^2)/8 = 3.1543175 agrees to 5e-7. Controls at N = 2x10^8: RANDM 3.141478 (-0.54 sigma), MINSTD 3.141395 (-0.93), MT19937 3.141333 (-1.23), RANNUM 3.141451 (-0.67). The exact RANDM full-period value is 3.1415987 (bias 6e-6).

findings.claim: The 4-sigma low ball estimate from RANDM's first 10^7 triplets (seed 777) is an isolated, unexplained excursion. It does not recur in other stretches of the sequence or with other seeds, and RANDM has no systematic bias or variance inflation for this integrand.
findings.evidence: The first 10^7 triplets give z = -4.03 (two-sided single-test p = 5.6e-5); 8 of its ten 10^6 sub-blocks are negative. The other 16 disjoint 10^7 blocks have z variance 0.55. Across 48 other seeds the z values have mean 0.21 and variance 0.71. Block dispersion D is 1.00, 0.97 and 0.98 for blocks of 10^4, 10^5 and 10^6 triplets; at 10^7 it is 1.63 (p = 0.052), driven by the first block alone. The full-period bias is 6e-6. Correcting for the 119 blocks examined (7 generators x 17) gives p of about 7e-3. Phase-shifting the triplets by 1 or 2 draws gives z = -2.3 and -2.1 on the same stretch of numbers, so this is a property of that stretch rather than of the triplet grouping.

findings.claim: All five LCGs have hyperplane structure; only its severity differs. Each well-known multiplier has a weak dimension: MINSTD (16807) in 2D, MINSTD2 (48271, the 'improved' Park-Miller multiplier) in 8D, where it is worse than 16807, and 69069 in 6D.
findings.evidence: MINSTD: S_2 = 0.338, with 16807 lines 16807x_k - x_{k+1} = j. MINSTD2: S_t >= 0.73 for t <= 6, but nu_8^2 = 82, which gives 23 planes, S_8 = 0.436 and mu_8 = 0.0855 (< 0.1); 16807 has S_8 = 0.610 with 27 planes. LCG69069: S_6 = 0.299 with 34 occupied planes and mu_6 = 0.0171; S_7 = 0.407 with mu_7 = 0.0705. All plane counts come from full-period enumeration.

findings.claim: Every test in this family was validated on MT19937 and RANNUM, and neither generator is flagged by any of them.
findings.evidence: Near-integer fraction of 9x-6y+z: 0.009956 and 0.009953 (expected 0.01). Killer integrands: all 16 z values within |z| <= 2.11. Structure factor maxima: 8.82 and 9.30. Isotropy chi-square: p = 0.20 for MT19937. Ball pi: -1.23 and -0.67 sigma. Block dispersion D between 0.83 and 1.13 (all p > 0.09). Edge-on projections show no planes.

figures.caption: Top: 12000 RANDU triplets seen from a generic angle (no structure visible), then rotated so that the viewing direction lies inside the planes (15 planes appear), next to MT19937 seen from the same direction. Bottom left: distribution of $9x_k-6x_{k+1}+x_{k+2}$ for $10^7$ triplets; all RANDU mass falls on the integers $-5$ to $9$, while MT19937 follows the continuous density $f_S$. Bottom right: the plane populations agree with the geometric shares $(1,3,5,7,9,11,12,12,12,\dots)/108$ ($\chi^2 = 11.6$, 14 dof, $p = 0.64$).

Left: exact normalized spectral figure of merit $S_t=\nu_t/(\gamma_t^{1/2}m^{1/t})$ for $t=2$ to 8. RANDU collapses at $t=3$ ($S_3=0.0095$) and RANDM is weakest at $t=2$ ($S_2=0.19$); open markers show the lower value obtained from the true largest gap after the coset correction. Right: number of hyperplanes in the shortest-dual-vector family that are actually occupied over the full period, compared with Marsaglia's bound $(t!\,m)^{1/t}$ for $m=2^{31}$ (the bound for LCG69069, with $m=2^{32}$, is larger by $2^{1/t}$).

Tuples projected onto the shortest dual vector $\mathbf{s}$ (horizontal) and an orthogonal direction (vertical), so that the covering hyperplanes are seen edge-on as vertical lines. Every LCG shows planes (RANDU 15 in 3D, RANDM 43 in 6D, MINSTD 27 and MINSTD2 23 in 8D, LCG69069 34 in 6D); MT19937 projected onto RANDM's 6D normal shows none.

Top: RANDM pairs with $x_k<3/6539$ lie exactly on the lines $x_{k+1}=6539x_k-j$ (the 2D weakness of RANDM), while MT19937 fills the same strip uniformly. Bottom: RANDM triplets in a slab eight plane spacings wide along $\mathbf{s}=(25,115,678)$ fall on 8 planes spaced $1/688$, so its 3D lattice is about 75 times finer than RANDU's.

Monte Carlo estimates of integrals $\int\cos 2\pi(\mathbf{s}\cdot\mathbf{x}-\varphi)\,d\mathbf{x}=0$ built from each LCG's shortest dual vector, versus the number of tuples $N$. The owning LCG returns exactly 1 with zero error bar at every $N$; MT19937 and RANNUM converge to 0 inside the $\pm 2/\sqrt{2N}$ band.

Structure factor of a simulated ideal gas of $10^5$ particles. RANDU positions produce a Bragg peak $S(9,-6,1)=N$ in the $n_3=1$ slice, which MT19937 does not. Right: over all 4630 wave vectors with $|n_i|\le 10$, every generator follows the ideal-gas law $P(S>s)=e^{-s}$, apart from RANDU's single point at $S=10^5$.

Top left: hit-or-miss estimate of $\pi$ from the volume of the unit ball; RANDU converges to the 15-plane quadrature value 3.15432 (dotted), not to $\pi$, while the other generators stay inside $\pm 2\sigma$. Top right and bottom: directions from cube rejection with RANDU follow the 15-plane sawtooth theory, with 13.8% of all directions exactly on one great circle and an empty belt $0<|\cos\theta|<2/\sqrt{118}$; the MT19937 sky map is uniform.

caveats: The nu_t^2 values for 69069 and 16807 are said to agree with Knuth's TAOCP Vol. 2, Table 1 of Sec. 3.3.4 from memory only; the book was not available to check them. The same applies to whether Knuth's text prescribes the modulus 2^{e-2} for a = 3 (mod 8). The student should check both before citing. Our own results do not depend on these citations: they rest on brute-force and full-period enumeration.

The plane counts in the figures and tables are for the family defined by the shortest dual vector. The minimal number of covering hyperplanes (minimal L1 norm over the dual lattice) was not computed in general and can be smaller. For example, RANDU in t >= 4 has a 15-plane family (9,-6,1,0,...), while its shortest-vector family has 17 planes.

For RANDU and RANDM, S_t is normalized with M = 2^30, the coset lattice. Normalizing by the 2^29 points actually visited would raise S_t by a factor 2^{1/t}. The 'true largest gap' S values in the figure use the same normalization.
The coset analysis assumes an odd seed. Even seeds, such as the student's seed 65536 case, shrink the period and the reachable set further and were not analysed here.

The structure-factor test only probes |n_i| <= 10, so it cannot see RANDM's or MINSTD's 3D lattices, whose shortest vectors have components up to 678 and 631. Those were probed directly with the killer integrals, which compute the same quantity.
The RANDM seed-777 first-block excursion in the ball estimate (z = -4.03) remains unexplained. The controls show it is not systematic, but we did not identify a mechanism.
The spectral test stops at t = 8 because the Hermite constants are known exactly only up to t = 8.

Planned but not done: blind recovery of the dual vector from output data alone (LLL on observed tuples); a 2D histogram test with more than 6539 bins per axis, which would show RANDM's lines in an ordinary histogram; and analysis of the course's own fixed-form RANDU and RANDM, whose single-precision constants .4656613E-9 and 1./IMAX are left to the 'hist' family.
About 12 CPU-minutes were used in total, most of it the full-period enumeration (8.4 min).
rnglib_issues: No bugs found. The local integer re-implementations of RANDU, RANDM and MINSTD matched rnglib's rng_state_int for 10^6 steps each. Full-period runs confirmed periods of 2^29 for RANDU and RANDM from seed 777 (state after P steps equals the start, state after P/2 steps does not) and 2^31-2 for MINSTD.

Usage note, not a bug: rng_init(G_RANDU or G_RANDM, seed) accepts seed 0, which yields a constant stream of zeros, and accepts even seeds, which shorten the period. There is no warning in either case.
